newsitem.title: CHINA: FOCUS-China B shares close down, pressured by HK.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-China B shares close down, pressured by HK.

text.p: China's hard currency B shares took a pounding on Tuesday, battered by a steep fall on Hong Kong's stock market where fears over the currency triggered a flurry of selling.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index skidded 619.62 points, or 3.85 percent to close at 15,477.26, sending prices tumbling on the neighbouring market of Shenzhen.

Shenzhen's B share index slumped 11.84 points or 7.46 percent to finish the day at 146.88 while turnover shrank to HK$310 million from last Friday's HK$700 million. Shenzhen's B share market was closed on Monday for a holiday.
"Shenzhen's B index is so easily hurt by Hong Kong's tumble because last week's B index surge was built on Hong Kong's market optimism," a broker at China Guotai Securities said.
Asian currencies, such as the Thai baht and the Indonesian rupiah, have been hit hard by speculators recently. Hong Kong has raised interbank rates to fend off currency speculators.

Shenzhen's B share index performed strongly at the end of last week, advancing on Thursday and Friday as investors were attracted by lower prices compared to those of H shares, or mainland shares listed in Hong Kong.
But Shenzhen B shares fell on profit-taking on Tuesday as investors returned from a three-day break and kicked off the morning by cashing in their recent gains, analysts said.
Shenzhen North Jianshe Motorcycle fell to its 10 percent limit-down level of HK$2.48 after reporting a 51 percent year-on-year decrease in first-half net profits.
Leading pesticide maker Hubei Sanonda Co was also hit by selling despite its announcement of a 44 percent year-on-year rise in its interim net profits. It lost HK$0.50 to HK$4.53.

Shenzhen's A share market was much quieter. It edged up a miniscule 0.04 point to 365.51, following the Shenzhen Development Bank's announcement that it would honour its original dividend plan. It was punished recently for trading its own stock.
The bank's shares rose 0.90 yuan to 31.41 yuan.
Shanghai's foreign currency B shares closed down nearly 4.6 percent on Tuesday, also feeling the pressure from Hong Kong.
Sharp falls on Tuesday in H shares hurt sentiment for China plays, causing investors to sell B shares in Shanghai, brokers said.
The B index lost 4.057 points or 4.59 percent to 84.367 on turnover of $22.54 million against $30.00 million on Monday.
Of Shanghai's 47 B share issues, 46 were traded on Tuesday with 43 of them losing ground. Two rose while one was unchanged.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Products was the biggest B share loser on Tuesday after announcing last week its first-half profits rose a lower-than-expected 5.8 percent.
It slid $0.098 or 9.86 percent to $0.896 on volume of nearly 2.9 million shares, making it the second most active stock.
Recently listed Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal was the most active B share as it war hit by profit-taking, brokers said. It fell $0.014 or 2.64 percent to $0.516.
Shanghai's domestic currency A shares dnddd the day down slightly il dull trade with most investors clinging to the sidelines.
The A index slipped 0.069 point or 0.01 percent to 1,179.373 on turnnver of 2.157 billion yuan against 2.750 billion on Monday.
